note: The fetch ledger and the sentence ledger of the gated-briefs package (docs/wave8-contracts.md, section 9). Each brief under infra/intake/briefs/ lists the pages it was written from; every page was fetched with WebFetch in the writing session, and the claims below are the sentences of a brief that restate a source, each with a locator and, for a regulation, a verbatim quote of 25 words or fewer. The remaining documents are page copy: the squeeze, hub and thanks copy module, the two page files and the open abstracts. Each sentence maps to one claim (C-nn), one existing page with a heading (path#heading) or one decision, or is a short control label. tests/unit/wp-63/copy-ledger.test.ts enumerates the sentences from the files that hold them, fails on one with no mapping and on a mapping with no sentence, and runs the claims denylist over all of them. Interface strings built at run time (the depth line under a card) hold a date and a count only and are denylist-scanned by that test.

What each way of paying for early work asks of the company in return
Seven ways to pay for early software work, compared by what each asks of the company: customers, awards, loans, shares, convertible instruments and crowds.
Founders are often shown funding as a menu, with the amount of money on offer as the only column.
This brief reads the same options from the other side and asks what each one requires of the company once the money has arrived.
It covers seven paths: revenue and savings, federal research awards, loans, private sales of shares, convertible instruments, priced rounds and regulated crowdfunding.
For each path it reports what a public source says the mechanism is, then separates that report from analysis of which kind of company the path tends to suit.
It also lists questions to put to any path before committing, and it sets out the limits of what its sources can show.
Those include rules that change, facts specific to your company and every jurisdiction outside the United States.
